page: Microsoft Azure F8as_v6 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Fasv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and text generation for small language models also demonstrate strong performance. Multi-core execution, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

The dedicated core allocation and high clock speed provide stable compute performance without hyper-threading overhead. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires external storage attachment, which may introduce latency depending on the configuration. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F8as_v6 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and light language model inference.
